name: Self-introduction at work
description: Phrases and patterns for introducing yourself, your role, your team and your company in NZ client meetings and kick-offs.

words.zh: 大家好，我是…（会议开场最常用）
words.definition: The simplest, most natural way to start your intro in a meeting.

examples.en: Hi everyone, I'm Alex, I'm one of the cloud engineers on this project.
examples.zh: 大家好，我是 Alex，是这个项目的云工程师之一。

words.note: 不用说 'My name is …'，在会上显得太正式；直接说 I'm … 就很自然。

words.zh: 大家好（毛利语问候，新西兰职场常用）
words.definition: A Māori greeting meaning 'hello everyone'. Very common at the start of meetings and presentations in New Zealand workplaces.

examples.en: Kia ora koutou, I'm Sam, and I'll be running the workshop today.
examples.zh: 大家好，我是 Sam，今天的研讨会由我主持。

words.note: kia ora 可以对一个人说；koutou 指三个人以上。新移民用也完全没问题，显得尊重本地文化，注意读音。

words.zh: 早上好（毛利语，早上开会时用）
words.definition: A Māori word for 'good morning', often used by Kiwis of all backgrounds to start a morning meeting.

examples.en: Mōrena, everyone. I'm Priya from the data team.
examples.zh: 大家早上好，我是数据团队的 Priya。

words.note: 只在上午用。说 Mōrena 后可以接英文正常介绍。

words.term: For those who don't know me, I'm …
words.zh: 不认识我的朋友，我是…（部分人已认识你时）
words.definition: Use this when some people in the room already know you and some don't.

examples.en: For those who don't know me, I'm Ben, I look after our Microsoft 365 support.
examples.zh: 不认识我的朋友，我是 Ben，负责我们的 Microsoft 365 支持。

words.term: Just a quick intro from me
words.zh: 我简单介绍一下自己（说明会很简短）
words.definition: Signals that your introduction will be short, which people appreciate in busy meetings.

examples.en: Just a quick intro from me: I'm Mia, I'm the project manager for the migration.
examples.zh: 我简单介绍一下：我是 Mia，迁移项目的项目经理。

words.zh: 我长话短说（时间紧或人多时）
words.definition: Tells the group you won't take much time, so they relax and listen.

examples.en: I'll keep it short, since we've got a lot to get through today.
examples.zh: 今天要讨论的内容很多，我就长话短说。

words.note: 也可以说 'I'll keep this brief'，意思一样。

words.zh: 我是…公司/团队的…（对外介绍带上公司名）
words.definition: The standard way to say your name and which company or team you're from.

examples.en: I'm Tom from the infrastructure team.
examples.zh: 我是基础架构团队的 Tom。

examples.en: Hi, I'm Lucy from Contoso, the integration partner.
examples.zh: 你好，我是集成合作伙伴 Contoso 的 Lucy。

words.note: 介绍公司用 from，不要说 'I'm Lucy of Contoso'。

words.term: My name's …, but everyone calls me …
words.zh: 我叫…，大家都叫我…（有英文名或昵称时）
words.definition: Useful when you have a formal name and a shorter name or English name people use.

examples.en: My name's Zhang Wei, but everyone calls me Will.
examples.zh: 我叫张伟，大家都叫我 Will。

words.note: 有英文名就直接告诉大家用哪个，省得别人不好意思叫你。

words.zh: 读作…（帮别人念对你的名字）
words.definition: Helps people say your name correctly, often by comparing it to an English word.

examples.en: I'm Wei, it's pronounced like 'way'.
examples.zh: 我叫 Wei，读音像 'way'。

words.note: 主动说读音很常见，也很受欢迎；对方会更有信心叫你的名字。

words.zh: 大家早（随意，团队内部会议）
words.definition: A short, casual greeting for a morning meeting with people you work with often.

examples.en: Morning all, I'm Jess, I'm filling in for Daniel today.
examples.zh: 大家早，我是 Jess，今天替 Daniel 来开会。

words.zh: 谢谢邀请我参加（作为外部人员出席时）
words.definition: A polite opener when you join someone else's meeting as a guest, consultant or vendor.

examples.en: Thanks for having me. I'm Raj, the solution architect from our side.
examples.zh: 谢谢邀请。我是 Raj，我们这边的解决方案架构师。

words.zh: 我先简单介绍一下自己
words.definition: A clear way to start your introduction when nobody has asked you to yet.

examples.en: Before we start, let me quickly introduce myself. I'm Alex, the lead engineer.
examples.zh: 开始之前，我先简单介绍一下，我是 Alex，主工程师。

words.term: Shall we do a quick round of intros?
words.zh: 我们轮流简单介绍一下吧？（主持会议时）
words.definition: Use this when you are running the meeting and want everyone to introduce themselves.

examples.en: Since a few of us are new, shall we do a quick round of intros?
examples.zh: 既然有几位是新来的，我们轮流简单介绍一下吧？

words.note: intros 是 introductions 的口语说法。

words.definition: Offers to start the round of introductions, which shows confidence and helps others relax.

examples.en: I'll go first. I'm Sam, I'm a data engineer here.
examples.zh: 我先来。我是 Sam，这里的数据工程师。

words.zh: 很高兴认识你（比 Nice to meet you 稍随意）
words.definition: A friendly, slightly more relaxed version of 'nice to meet you', common in NZ.

examples.en: Good to meet you, Jess. I've heard great things about your team.
examples.zh: 很高兴认识你，Jess。早就听说你们团队很棒。

words.note: Kiwis 一般只说一次 Nice/Good to meet you；对方先说了，你回 'You too' 就行。

words.term: Hi, I'm … — I don't think we've met
words.zh: 你好，我是…，我们好像还没见过（主动认识人）
words.definition: A friendly way to introduce yourself to someone one-on-one before or after a meeting.

examples.en: Hi, I'm Priya — I don't think we've met. Are you on the finance side?
examples.zh: 你好，我是 Priya，我们好像还没见过。你是财务那边的吗？

words.definition: The basic pattern for your job title and employer.

examples.en: I'm a cloud engineer at a Microsoft partner in Auckland.
examples.zh: 我是奥克兰一家微软合作伙伴公司的云工程师。

words.note: 职位前要加 a/an：I'm a data engineer，不要说 'I'm data engineer'。

words.definition: Says which team you belong to, which helps people understand who to come to.

examples.en: I work in the platform team, so anything to do with Azure goes through us.
examples.zh: 我在平台团队，所以跟 Azure 相关的事都经过我们。

words.note: 新西兰公司多说 team，较少说 department；用 in the … team。

words.definition: Shows you belong to a team; slightly softer than 'I work in'.

examples.en: I'm part of the data and analytics team.
examples.zh: 我是数据分析团队的一员。

words.zh: 我负责带领…（部门或团队负责人）
words.definition: Means you lead a team or area. Common and confident without sounding bossy.

examples.en: I head up the service desk, so I've got a team of eight.
examples.zh: 我负责服务台，带一个八人团队。

words.note: head up = lead，比 'I'm the boss of …' 自然得多。

words.definition: A direct way to say you are the leader of a team.

examples.en: I lead the security team, and I'll be joining a few of these sessions.
examples.zh: 我带安全团队，会参加其中几场会议。

words.zh: 我是这里的…之一（同岗位有好几个人时）
words.definition: Use this when there are several people with the same role, so you don't sound like the only one.

examples.en: I'm one of the solution architects here.
examples.zh: 我是这里的解决方案架构师之一。

words.note: 后面用复数：one of the engineers，不要说 one of the engineer。

words.definition: A simple way to explain that you've only just started.

examples.en: I'm new to the team, so I'm still getting my head around everything.
examples.zh: 我刚加入团队，还在熟悉各种情况。

words.note: get my head around = 弄明白、熟悉；比 'I don't know anything yet' 更积极。

words.definition: Says your new role and that you started recently.

examples.en: I've just joined as a business analyst, so this is my first project here.
examples.zh: 我刚加入当业务分析师，这是我在这里的第一个项目。

words.definition: Tells people who your manager is, which helps them see where you fit.

examples.en: I report to Sarah, our head of delivery.
examples.zh: 我向我们的交付负责人 Sarah 汇报。

words.zh: 我隶属于…（说明在组织中的位置）
words.definition: Explains which part of the organisation your role belongs to.

examples.en: I sit within the infrastructure group, but I work closely with the developers.
examples.zh: 我隶属于基础架构组，但和开发人员合作很紧密。

words.term: My title is …, but basically I …
words.zh: 我的头衔是…，其实主要是…（头衔听起来模糊时）
words.definition: Use this when your job title doesn't explain much, then say what you actually do.

examples.en: My title is technical consultant, but basically I help clients move their servers to the cloud.
examples.zh: 我的头衔是技术顾问，其实主要是帮客户把服务器迁到云上。

words.term: I'm on the … side of things
words.definition: A relaxed way to say which area of the work you cover.

examples.en: I'm on the infrastructure side of things, so networks, servers and backups.
examples.zh: 我做基础架构这块，就是网络、服务器和备份。

words.zh: 我在…工作（with ＝ 在某公司/团队）
words.definition: A short, natural way to say which company or group you work for.

examples.en: Hi, I'm Ben, I'm with Contoso — we're the implementation partner.
examples.zh: 你好，我是 Ben，在 Contoso 工作，我们是实施合作伙伴。

words.zh: 我同时负责多个…（跨团队或项目）
words.definition: Means your work covers several teams, clients or projects rather than just one.

examples.en: I work across a few of our bigger accounts, including this one.
examples.zh: 我同时负责我们几个较大的客户，包括这一个。

words.definition: Says where you normally work, useful when the team is spread across cities.

examples.en: I'm based in the Wellington office, but I'm up in Auckland most weeks.
examples.zh: 我在惠灵顿办公室，不过大多数星期都会来奥克兰。

words.note: NZ 说去北边城市用 up，去南边用 down：up in Auckland, down in Christchurch。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.zh: 我负责…（最自然的“负责”说法）
words.definition: A natural, everyday way to say what you are responsible for.

examples.en: I look after our Azure environment and the backups.
examples.zh: 我负责我们的 Azure 环境和备份。

words.note: look after 比 be responsible for 更口语，新西兰人很常用。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: A more formal way to say a task or area is your job.

examples.en: I'm responsible for making sure the data pipelines run on time.
examples.zh: 我负责确保数据管道按时运行。

words.note: 后面接名词或 -ing：responsible for managing，不要说 'responsible to manage'。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Says you handle a task so others don't have to worry about it.

examples.en: I take care of user accounts and access requests.
examples.zh: 我处理用户账户和权限申请。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Gives the main part of your job in one sentence.

examples.en: My role is mainly about designing the solution and making sure it fits your needs.
examples.zh: 我的工作主要是设计方案，并确保它符合你们的需求。

words.term: I spend most of my time …
words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Describes what you actually do most days, which is often clearer than a job title.

examples.en: I spend most of my time building reports in Power BI.
examples.zh: 我大部分时间在用 Power BI 做报表。

words.note: spend time doing，不要说 'spend time to do'。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Describes your job in terms of who you help, which sounds friendly and useful.

examples.en: I help customers with their move to the cloud.
examples.zh: 我帮客户迁移到云端。

words.note: 两种结构：help sb with sth / help sb do sth。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Means people usually come to you for a certain kind of question or problem.

examples.en: I'm the go-to person for anything to do with networking.
examples.zh: 网络相关的问题找我就对了。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Means you have several roles at once, common in smaller companies.

examples.en: We're a small team, so I wear a few hats: support, projects, and a bit of security.
examples.zh: 我们团队小，所以我身兼数职：支持、项目，还有一点安全。

words.term: A big part of my job is …
words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Highlights the most important part of your work.

examples.en: A big part of my job is talking to users and working out what they really need.
examples.zh: 我工作很大一部分是跟用户沟通，弄清他们真正需要什么。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Introduces what your normal working day looks like.

examples.en: Day to day, I'm mostly working on tickets and small improvements.
examples.zh: 日常来说，我主要处理工单和做一些小改进。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Shows who you collaborate with, which helps people see your place in the team.

examples.en: I work closely with the developers to get changes into production.
examples.zh: 我和开发人员密切合作，把变更发布到生产环境。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: A plain way to say which issues or tasks you handle.

examples.en: I deal with most of the escalations from the service desk.
examples.zh: 服务台升级上来的问题大多由我处理。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Says you are in charge of a system, a budget or a group of people.

examples.en: I manage our Microsoft 365 tenant and the licensing.
examples.zh: 我管理我们的 Microsoft 365 租户和许可证。

words.note: manage 对人 = 管人，对系统 = 管理维护；说清楚是哪种。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: A simple, clear way to describe support or operations work.

examples.en: I keep the servers and network running for about three hundred staff.
examples.zh: 我负责让大约三百名员工使用的服务器和网络正常运转。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Describes the result you are responsible for, not just the tasks.

examples.en: I make sure our releases go out smoothly and nothing breaks.
examples.zh: 我确保我们的发布顺利上线，不出问题。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.zh: 我掌握/了解…的情况（澳新常用）
words.definition: Australian and NZ English for knowing about something and keeping up to date with it.

examples.en: I'm across all the reporting work, so feel free to ask me about it.
examples.zh: 报表方面的工作我都清楚，有问题可以问我。

words.note: be across sth 是澳新特色用法 = 了解并跟进某事，听到别听懵了。

words.topic: What you do day to day
words.definition: Gives your main work plus a smaller extra area, in a relaxed way.

examples.en: Mostly Azure infrastructure, with a bit of PowerShell scripting.
examples.zh: 主要做 Azure 基础架构，也写一些 PowerShell 脚本。

words.definition: Explains what you will do on this specific project, not just your general job.

examples.en: On this project, I'll be setting up the landing zone and the networking.
examples.zh: 在这个项目里，我会负责搭建 landing zone 和网络。

words.term: I'll be your main point of contact for …
words.zh: …方面我是你们的主要联系人
words.definition: Tells the client who to talk to first about a certain area.

examples.en: I'll be your main point of contact for anything technical.
examples.zh: 技术方面的事我是你们的主要联系人。

words.note: point of contact 常缩写 POC，但口头一般说全称。

words.definition: Shows who you will work with, often the client's own staff.

examples.en: I'll be working alongside your IT team during the migration.
examples.zh: 迁移期间我会和你们的 IT 团队一起工作。

words.definition: States your purpose in the meeting or project clearly.

examples.en: I'm here to help you get the most out of the new platform.
examples.zh: 我来是为了帮你们充分用好新平台。

words.term: Today I'm mostly here to listen
words.zh: 今天我主要是来听的（需求调研或第一次见面）
words.definition: Shows the client you want to understand them before you suggest anything.

examples.en: Today I'm mostly here to listen and understand how things work for you now.
examples.zh: 今天我主要是来听听，了解你们现在的工作方式。

words.definition: Says which part of the work you will concentrate on.

examples.en: My focus will be on security and making sure everything meets your policies.
examples.zh: 我的重点会放在安全上，确保一切符合你们的政策。

words.zh: 你们可能会在…见到我（哪些会议或场合）
words.definition: Tells people where they will run into you during the project.

examples.en: You'll probably see me in the weekly stand-ups and the design sessions.
examples.zh: 你们可能会在每周站会和设计讨论会上见到我。

words.term: I'll be looking after the technical side
words.definition: A clear way to split roles, often said next to a project manager.

examples.en: Mia's running the project, and I'll be looking after the technical side.
examples.zh: Mia 负责管理项目，技术方面由我负责。

words.definition: Says you will be in charge of a piece of work.

examples.en: I'll be leading the testing, so I'll reach out to book some time with your users.
examples.zh: 我会牵头测试工作，之后会联系你们的用户约时间。

words.definition: Describes a support role, where someone else leads and you help.

examples.en: I'll be supporting Raj with the data migration.
examples.zh: 我会协助 Raj 做数据迁移。

words.term: I'll be doing most of the hands-on work
words.zh: 大部分具体实施工作由我来做
words.definition: Tells the client you are the person actually building or configuring things.

examples.en: Tom will do the design, and I'll be doing most of the hands-on work.
examples.zh: Tom 负责设计，大部分具体实施由我来做。

words.definition: Points out a specific task you will personally do.

examples.en: I'll be the one setting up your accounts, so you'll get an email from me.
examples.zh: 你们的账户会由我来开，所以你们会收到我的邮件。

words.term: Anything to do with …, just come to me
words.definition: Invites people to bring a certain kind of question straight to you.

examples.en: Anything to do with access or licences, just come to me.
examples.zh: 跟权限或许可证有关的事，直接找我。

words.term: I'll be with you from … through to …
words.zh: 我会从…一直跟到…（项目阶段）
words.definition: Explains how long you will be involved in the project.

examples.en: I'll be with you from discovery through to go-live.
examples.zh: 我会从需求调研一直跟到上线。

words.note: go-live = 上线，discovery = 前期调研，都是项目常用词。

words.term: Once …, I'll be handing over to …
words.definition: Tells the client who will take over from you later, so there are no surprises.

examples.en: Once we go live, I'll be handing over to our support team.
examples.zh: 上线之后我会交接给我们的支持团队。

words.term: My job is to make sure …
words.definition: Describes your role by the outcome you protect.

examples.en: My job is to make sure nothing gets lost when we move your data across.
examples.zh: 我的任务是确保数据迁移过程中不丢任何东西。

words.term: I'll be your … for this engagement
words.zh: 这次合作中我担任你们的…
words.definition: A formal, consulting-style way to give your role on a client project.

examples.en: I'll be your technical lead for this engagement.
examples.zh: 这次合作中我担任你们的技术负责人。

words.note: engagement 在咨询行业 = 一次合作或项目，不是“订婚”。

words.zh: 我是…出身的（说明专业背景）
words.definition: Tells people which field you come from.

examples.en: My background is in networking, but these days I do mostly cloud work.
examples.zh: 我是做网络出身的，不过现在主要做云。

words.term: I've been working in … for about … years
words.definition: Gives your experience in a field, using the present perfect continuous.

examples.en: I've been working in IT for about twelve years.
examples.zh: 我在 IT 行业工作大约十二年了。

words.note: 用现在完成进行时；不要说 'I work in IT for 12 years'。

words.definition: Links your current job to your previous one.

examples.en: Before joining the team, I was a developer at a bank.
examples.zh: 加入团队之前，我在一家银行做开发。

words.note: joining 用 -ing；也可说 Before I joined …。

words.term: I've worked on a few similar projects
words.zh: 我做过几个类似的项目
words.definition: Builds trust by showing you have relevant experience, without overselling.

examples.en: I've worked on a few similar projects, so I've got a good idea of where the tricky bits are.
examples.zh: 我做过几个类似的项目，所以大概知道难点在哪儿。

words.note: 实事求是：只有一两个就说 a couple，别夸大。

words.term: I've done a lot of work with …
words.definition: Highlights a tool, technology or type of client you know well.

examples.en: I've done a lot of work with Power BI and Fabric.
examples.zh: 我在 Power BI 和 Fabric 方面做过很多工作。

words.zh: 我是从…转行做 IT 的
words.definition: Explains a career change, which is common and often interesting to people.

examples.en: I came into IT from accounting, so I understand the finance side quite well.
examples.zh: 我是从会计转行做 IT 的，所以比较懂财务这块。

words.term: I moved to New Zealand from … in …
words.definition: A simple personal detail that helps people connect with you.

examples.en: I moved to New Zealand from China in 2018, and I've been in Auckland ever since.
examples.zh: 我 2018 年从中国搬来新西兰，之后一直在奥克兰。

words.note: 客户会议里点到为止，一句就够，不用讲移民经历。

words.definition: Describes the first job in your career, often to show how you've grown.

examples.en: I started out as a support engineer on the service desk.
examples.zh: 我最早是在服务台做支持工程师。

words.term: Most of my experience is in …
words.definition: Says where your strongest experience is.

examples.en: Most of my experience is in government and healthcare.
examples.zh: 我的经验主要在政府和医疗行业。

words.definition: Describes what you have been doing recently in your career.

examples.en: I've spent the last five years helping companies move off old on-prem servers.
examples.zh: 过去五年我一直在帮企业迁移掉老旧的本地服务器。

words.definition: Says how long you have been with your current company.

examples.en: I've been here for about two years now.
examples.zh: 我在这里差不多两年了。

words.note: 不要说 'I am here for two years'。

words.definition: A slightly formal way to mention your previous role.

examples.en: Prior to that, I was a BI developer for a retail company.
examples.zh: 在那之前，我在一家零售公司做 BI 开发。

words.definition: Mentions a professional certification when it is relevant to the client.

examples.en: I'm certified in Azure, mainly on the infrastructure and security side.
examples.zh: 我有 Azure 认证，主要是基础架构和安全方向。

words.note: 只说和这次项目相关的认证，不要一口气列一长串。

words.definition: Talks about your experience in another country or an earlier time.

examples.en: Back in China, I worked as a developer for an e-commerce company.
examples.zh: 以前在中国的时候，我在一家电商公司做开发。

words.definition: Shows the range of industries or areas you have worked in.

examples.en: I've worked across banking, retail and local government.
examples.zh: 我在银行、零售和地方政府都做过。

words.term: I've seen it from both sides
words.zh: 我两边都经历过（如甲方和乙方）
words.definition: Means you have been both the client and the supplier, which helps you understand the client.

examples.en: I've been on the client side too, so I've seen it from both sides.
examples.zh: 我也在甲方做过，所以两边都经历过。

words.note: client side = 甲方，vendor/partner side = 乙方。

words.zh: 我很喜欢亲自动手（不只是动嘴）
words.definition: Means you like doing the actual work, not just managing or advising.

examples.en: I'm pretty hands-on, so I'll be in the portal with your team, not just in meetings.
examples.zh: 我很喜欢亲自动手，会跟你们团队一起在后台操作，而不只是开会。

words.definition: Shares what you like about your work, which shows passion without bragging.

examples.en: I enjoy solving the messy problems that no one else wants to touch.
examples.zh: 我喜欢解决那些别人都不想碰的棘手问题。

words.note: enjoy 后接 -ing，不接 to do。

words.definition: Names a strength, and 'I'd say' keeps it modest and natural.

examples.en: I'm good at explaining technical stuff to non-technical people, I'd say.
examples.zh: 我觉得我挺擅长向非技术人员解释技术问题。

words.note: I'd say 让语气温和，既不夸张也不过分谦虚。

words.term: One thing I really like is …
words.definition: Shares something you value in your work, which makes you more relatable.

examples.en: One thing I really like is seeing users actually enjoy a system we've built.
examples.zh: 我特别喜欢看到用户真正喜欢我们做的系统。

words.zh: 我喜欢把…变简单，让…容易用/理解
words.definition: A friendly strength that clients value: making complex things easy.

examples.en: I like making complex tech simple for the people who have to use it.
examples.zh: 我喜欢把复杂的技术变简单，让真正使用的人容易上手。

words.zh: 我专注于…（代替 I'm just a …）
words.definition: A confident way to describe your area without making yourself sound small.

examples.en: I focus on testing, so I'll make sure everything works before it reaches your users.
examples.zh: 我专注于测试，会确保一切在交给用户前都正常。

words.note: 不要说 'I'm just a developer' 或 'I only do testing'；just/only 会显得没自信，直接说你做什么。

words.term: I've had a fair bit of experience with …
words.definition: Says you have solid experience, in a calm Kiwi way.

examples.en: I've had a fair bit of experience with SharePoint migrations.
examples.zh: 我在 SharePoint 迁移方面有不少经验。

words.note: a fair bit = 相当多，比 'I'm an expert in …' 谦和自然。

words.definition: Means you are comfortable and experienced with a tool or system.

examples.en: I know my way around Intune, so I can help with the device setup.
examples.zh: 我对 Intune 很熟，可以帮忙做设备配置。

words.term: English is my second language, so …
words.zh: 英语是我的第二语言，所以…（主动说明，不道歉）
words.definition: A confident way to mention your English and invite people to check with you.

examples.en: English is my second language, so feel free to stop me if anything's unclear.
examples.zh: 英语是我的第二语言，有不清楚的地方随时打断我。

words.note: 不要一开口就道歉 'Sorry, my English is poor'，会削弱专业形象；很多时候根本不需要提。

words.zh: 我还在学…，不过…（坦诚但不贬低自己）
words.definition: Admits a gap honestly while showing you can still help.

examples.en: I'm still learning the finance side, but I know the system really well.
examples.zh: 财务这块我还在学，不过这个系统我很熟。

words.term: I'm happy to get stuck in
words.definition: A Kiwi phrase meaning you are keen to start working hard right away.

examples.en: Whatever needs doing, I'm happy to get stuck in.
examples.zh: 有什么需要做的，我都乐意直接上手。

words.note: get stuck in 是新西兰常用说法 = 撸起袖子开干。

words.definition: A casual way to say something matters a lot to you at work.

examples.en: I'm big on documentation, so you'll get a proper handover at the end.
examples.zh: 我很重视文档，所以最后会给你们完整的交接。

words.definition: Names a useful strength in a modest way; 'quite' softens it.

examples.en: I'm quite detail-oriented, which helps a lot with data migrations.
examples.zh: 我比较注重细节，这在数据迁移中很有帮助。

words.term: I'm a bit of a … nerd
words.zh: 我算是个…迷（自嘲式表达热情）
words.definition: Shows enthusiasm with a little self-humour, which Kiwis like.

examples.en: I'm a bit of a data nerd, so I'm really keen to dig into your reports.
examples.zh: 我算是个数据迷，很想深入看看你们的报表。

words.note: nerd 在这里是褒义的自嘲，不是贬义。

words.definition: Describes yourself positively but humbly.

examples.en: I like to think I'm pretty easy to work with.
examples.zh: 我自认为还算挺好合作的。

words.term: I've got a good handle on …
words.definition: Says you understand something well without claiming to be the best.

examples.en: I've got a good handle on your current setup after the assessment.
examples.zh: 评估之后，我对你们现在的环境掌握得不错。

words.note: 不要说 'I'm the best at …' 或 'I know everything about …'；在新西兰会被看作自大（tall poppy 文化）。

words.term: I like to keep things practical
words.definition: Tells the client you focus on what works rather than theory or buzzwords.

examples.en: I like to keep things practical, so we'll start with what gives you the most value.
examples.zh: 我喜欢务实，所以我们先从价值最大的部分做起。

words.term: Really looking forward to working with you all
words.definition: A warm, standard line to show you are happy to start working together.

examples.en: Really looking forward to working with you all on this.
examples.zh: 很期待在这个项目上和大家合作。

words.note: looking forward to 后接 -ing：working，不要说 to work。

words.definition: Shows interest in the client's situation; 'keen' is very common in NZ.

examples.en: Keen to hear about what's been working well and what hasn't.
examples.zh: 很想听听哪些做得好，哪些不太行。

words.note: keen 是新西兰超常用词 = 很想、很乐意。

words.definition: A friendly way to show you know a bit about the client or a person already.

examples.en: I've heard a lot about the new customer portal, so I'm keen to see it.
examples.zh: 早就听说新的客户门户了，很想看看。

words.note: 说 'I've heard a lot about you' 时最好跟一句具体的，否则听起来客套。

words.term: Feel free to reach out anytime
words.definition: Invites people to contact you whenever they need something.

examples.en: If anything comes up, feel free to reach out anytime.
examples.zh: 有什么事随时联系我。

words.note: reach out = 联系，职场常用。

words.definition: Offers help in a friendly, low-pressure way.

examples.en: Happy to help with any questions about the new setup.
examples.zh: 关于新环境的任何问题，我都很乐意帮忙。

words.definition: Means people can come to you at any time; used even when you don't have an office.

examples.en: My door's always open, even if it's a virtual one.
examples.zh: 随时欢迎来找我，哪怕是“线上的门”。

words.zh: 直接在 Teams 上找我
words.definition: A casual way to tell people the quickest way to reach you.

examples.en: If you get stuck, just ping me on Teams.
examples.zh: 遇到问题直接在 Teams 上找我。

words.note: ping = 发个消息找某人，IT 圈很常用。

words.definition: Thanks busy people for coming to the meeting.

examples.en: Thanks for making the time, I know it's a busy week for you.
examples.zh: 感谢抽时间过来，我知道这周你们很忙。

words.term: It's great to be involved in …
words.definition: Shows you are glad to be part of the client's project.

examples.en: It's great to be involved in something that'll make such a difference for your staff.
examples.zh: 很高兴能参与这个对你们员工影响这么大的项目。

words.term: I know you've been … for a while
words.zh: 我知道你们…已经有一段时间了（表达理解）
words.definition: Shows empathy for the client's problem before talking about solutions.

examples.en: I know you've been dealing with these outages for a while, so we want to get that sorted quickly.
examples.zh: 我知道你们被这些故障困扰一段时间了，所以我们想尽快解决。

words.definition: A polite, curious way to ask about the client's world.

examples.en: I'd love to understand how your team uses the current system day to day.
examples.zh: 我很想了解你们团队日常是怎么用现在这个系统的。

words.term: No question is a silly question
words.definition: Encourages people, especially non-technical staff, to ask anything.

examples.en: Please ask as you go. No question is a silly question.
examples.zh: 有问题随时问，没有什么问题是傻问题。

words.definition: Encourages people to do something, like ask questions or give feedback.

examples.en: Don't hesitate to tell us if something isn't working for you.
examples.zh: 如果有什么不合适，尽管告诉我们。

words.term: How long have you been in your role?
words.zh: 您做这个岗位多久了？（反问对方，建立联系）
words.definition: A simple question that turns your intro into a conversation.

examples.en: Nice to meet you, Jess. How long have you been in your role?
examples.zh: 很高兴认识你，Jess。你做这个岗位多久了？

words.term: It'd be great to hear a bit about your role too
words.definition: Invites the client to introduce themselves after you, which makes the meeting two-way.

examples.en: That's me. It'd be great to hear a bit about your role too.
examples.zh: 我就介绍到这。也很想听听您的角色。

words.term: We're all on the same team here
words.zh: 我们是一个团队（拉近双方距离）
words.definition: Shows you see the client as a partner, not as 'us and them'.

examples.en: We're all on the same team here, so let's work it out together.
examples.zh: 我们是一个团队，一起把问题解决。

words.term: I'm really excited about this one
words.zh: 这个项目我真的很期待
words.definition: Shows genuine enthusiasm for the project.

examples.en: I'm really excited about this one. It's a great chance to tidy things up.
examples.zh: 这个项目我真的很期待，是个整理优化的好机会。

words.note: 新西兰人语气偏低调，excited 说一次就好，别像推销。

words.term: We're a … company that helps … with …
words.zh: 我们是一家帮…做…的…公司
words.definition: A one-sentence company intro: what kind of company, who you help and with what.

examples.en: We're a cloud services company that helps businesses with their move to Azure.
examples.zh: 我们是一家云服务公司，帮企业迁移到 Azure。

words.note: 公司介绍一句话说清楚：类型＋客户＋做什么，别背官网口号。

words.definition: Says what your company is best known for or focuses on.

examples.en: We specialise in data platforms and reporting.
examples.zh: 我们专门做数据平台和报表。

words.note: 新西兰用英式拼写 specialise；美式是 specialize。

words.definition: Shows an existing relationship, which builds trust.

examples.en: We've been working with your team for about three years now, mostly on support.
examples.zh: 我们和你们团队合作大约三年了，主要是支持服务。

words.definition: Says where your company is located.

examples.en: We're based in Auckland, but we work with clients all over the country.
examples.zh: 我们在奥克兰，但客户遍布全国。

words.definition: Lists your company's locations.

examples.en: We've got offices in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch.
examples.zh: 我们在奥克兰、惠灵顿和基督城都有办公室。

words.definition: Gives a rough size of your company or team.

examples.en: We're a team of about forty, so it's a pretty close-knit group.
examples.zh: 我们团队大约四十人，大家关系挺紧密的。

words.note: 说实际人数，不确定就说 a small team / a mid-sized team。

words.definition: Says your company is an official partner of a big vendor, which explains your expertise.

examples.en: We're a Microsoft partner, so most of our work is on Azure and Microsoft 365.
examples.zh: 我们是微软合作伙伴，所以大部分工作在 Azure 和 Microsoft 365 上。

words.definition: Tells the client what your company mainly does.

examples.en: Our main focus is managed services: we look after IT for businesses that don't want to do it themselves.
examples.zh: 我们主要做托管服务：替那些不想自己管 IT 的企业打理 IT。

words.definition: Says what kind of clients your company usually works with.

examples.en: We work mostly with mid-sized NZ businesses and a few councils.
examples.zh: 我们主要服务新西兰中型企业和几个地方议会。

words.zh: 您可能是通过…知道我们的
words.definition: Connects your company to something the client may already have seen.

examples.en: You might know us from the support work we've been doing for your finance team.
examples.zh: 您可能是通过我们给你们财务团队做的支持工作知道我们的。

words.zh: 我们为…做过类似的项目
words.definition: Shows relevant experience by mentioning past clients or types of clients.

examples.en: We've done similar work for a couple of large retailers.
examples.zh: 我们为几家大型零售商做过类似的项目。

words.note: 提客户名前先确认可以公开；不确定就用 a large retailer 这类泛称。

words.definition: Explains what makes your company different from others.

examples.en: What sets us apart is that the same people who design it also support it.
examples.zh: 我们的不同之处在于，设计的人也就是后期支持的人。

words.note: 一句话就好，说多了像推销。

words.term: We look after … end to end
words.definition: Means your company handles the whole process, from start to finish.

examples.en: We look after the whole thing end to end, from design to day-to-day support.
examples.zh: 我们从设计到日常支持全程负责。

words.term: We've been around for about … years
words.zh: 我们公司成立大约…年了
words.definition: A casual way to say how long your company has existed.

examples.en: We've been around for about fifteen years, so we've seen a lot of changes in IT.
examples.zh: 我们公司成立大约十五年了，见证了 IT 的很多变化。

words.zh: 我们是新西兰本土公司
words.definition: Says your company is owned in New Zealand, which some clients value.

examples.en: We're a Kiwi-owned business, and all our support is done locally.
examples.zh: 我们是新西兰本土公司，所有支持都在本地完成。

words.note: 只有在属实时才说；Kiwi 指新西兰（人）。

words.definition: Introduces a colleague with one useful detail about their role.

examples.en: This is Raj, who'll be doing most of the build work.
examples.zh: 这位是 Raj，大部分搭建工作由他来做。

words.definition: A clear way to start introducing someone else.

examples.en: Let me introduce Mia, our project manager.
examples.zh: 我来介绍一下我们的项目经理 Mia。

words.definition: Hands the floor to others so they can introduce themselves.

examples.en: I'll let the rest of the team introduce themselves.
examples.zh: 让团队其他人自己介绍一下吧。

words.note: themselves 用于不指定性别或多人，很自然。

words.definition: A short, natural way to hand the conversation to the next person.

examples.en: That's me. Over to you, Ben.
examples.zh: 我说完了。Ben，交给你了。

words.definition: Explains a colleague's responsibility on the project.

examples.en: Jess will be looking after your training and user support.
examples.zh: Jess 会负责你们的培训和用户支持。

words.definition: Checks whether two people already know each other.

examples.en: You've met Tom, haven't you? He was at the workshop last month.
examples.zh: 你见过 Tom 吧？上个月的研讨会他也在。

words.zh: 我想介绍你认识…（较正式，一对一）
words.definition: A polite way to introduce one person to another.

examples.en: Sarah, I'd like you to meet Daniel, our lead developer.
examples.zh: Sarah，我想介绍你认识我们的首席开发 Daniel。

words.definition: A friendly way to say a colleague is the team's expert in something.

examples.en: Tom is our resident security guru, so he'll answer the tricky questions.
examples.zh: Tom 是我们这儿的安全大神，难题交给他回答。

words.note: resident 在这里是“本团队的”，带点幽默。

words.definition: Shows a colleague knows something very well, which builds the client's confidence.

examples.en: Priya knows your data warehouse inside out.
examples.zh: Priya 对你们的数据仓库了如指掌。

words.definition: Passes the speaking turn to someone else, often for the next part of the agenda.

examples.en: I'll hand over to Lucy, who'll walk you through the timeline.
examples.zh: 我交给 Lucy，她会带大家看一下时间表。

words.term: Do you two know each other?
words.definition: A friendly question before introducing two people.

examples.en: Do you two know each other? Jess, this is Sam from the data team.
examples.zh: 你们俩认识吗？Jess，这位是数据团队的 Sam。

words.definition: Introduces a guest politely and thanks them for coming.

examples.en: Mia from our security team has kindly joined us today.
examples.zh: 我们安全团队的 Mia 今天特意来参加。

words.definition: Explains that someone expected is absent.

examples.en: Unfortunately Daniel couldn't make it today, but I'll fill him in afterwards.
examples.zh: 遗憾的是 Daniel 今天来不了，会后我会跟他同步。

words.note: fill sb in = 给某人补充信息、同步情况。

words.definition: Keeps a round of introductions moving.

examples.en: Thanks, Raj. Who'd like to go next?
examples.zh: 谢谢 Raj。谁下一个？

words.definition: Checks that everyone has been introduced before moving on.

examples.en: Have I missed anyone? Great, let's get started.
examples.zh: 有我漏掉的人吗？好，那我们开始吧。

words.term: Sorry, I'm just coming off mute
words.definition: Explains a short delay before you start speaking on a call.

examples.en: Sorry, I'm just coming off mute. Hi everyone, I'm Alex.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我刚取消静音。大家好，我是 Alex。

words.definition: A casual way to say you are turning your video on.

examples.en: I'll pop my camera on so you can see who you're talking to.
examples.zh: 我把摄像头打开，让大家看看是谁在说话。

words.note: pop 在新西兰英语里常表示“快速放/开一下”，很口语。

words.definition: Checks your audio before you start.

examples.en: Can everyone hear me OK? Great, I'll get started.
examples.zh: 大家能听清吗？好，那我开始了。

words.definition: Says where you are joining the call from.

examples.en: I'm dialling in from our Christchurch office today.
examples.zh: 我今天在基督城办公室接入。

words.note: 英式拼写 dialling；美式 dialing。

words.term: I'll drop my details in the chat
words.zh: 我把联系方式发在聊天框里
words.definition: Offers your email or phone number in the meeting chat.

examples.en: I'll drop my details in the chat in case anyone needs to reach me.
examples.zh: 我把联系方式发在聊天框里，方便大家找我。

words.definition: Tells someone politely that nobody can hear them.

examples.en: Sorry, Sam, I think you're on mute.
examples.zh: 抱歉 Sam，你好像静音了。

words.term: You cut out for a second
words.definition: Tells someone their audio dropped so you missed part of what they said.

examples.en: Sorry, you cut out for a second there. Could you say that again?
examples.zh: 抱歉，你刚才声音断了一下，能再说一遍吗？

words.definition: Warns people that your audio or video might drop.

examples.en: My connection's a bit patchy today, so let me know if I freeze.
examples.zh: 我今天网络不太稳，如果卡住了请告诉我。

words.note: patchy = 时好时坏，新西兰常用来形容网络或天气。

words.term: I'll turn my camera off to save bandwidth
words.zh: 我关掉摄像头省点带宽
words.definition: Explains why you are switching your video off.

examples.en: I'll turn my camera off to save bandwidth, but I'm still here.
examples.zh: 我关掉摄像头省点带宽，不过我还在线。

words.term: Is my screen coming through OK?
words.zh: 大家能看到我的屏幕吗？
words.definition: Checks that others can see your shared screen.

examples.en: Is my screen coming through OK? You should see a diagram.
examples.zh: 大家能看到我的屏幕吗？应该能看到一张图。

words.definition: Tells people you are about to show something on screen.

examples.en: I'll just share my screen and show you a quick overview.
examples.zh: 我共享一下屏幕，给大家快速看个概览。

words.term: Hi to everyone in the room
words.zh: 会议室里的各位好（线上加线下的混合会议）
words.definition: Greets the people sitting together in a meeting room while you join online.

examples.en: Hi to everyone in the room, and to those online as well.
examples.zh: 会议室里的各位好，也问候线上的朋友们。

words.term: Just a quick intro for those on the call
words.zh: 给线上的朋友简单介绍一下
words.definition: Makes sure people who joined online also know who you are.

examples.en: Just a quick intro for those on the call: I'm Ben, the delivery lead.
examples.zh: 给线上的朋友简单介绍一下：我是 Ben，交付负责人。

words.zh: 抱歉，您先说（两人同时开口时）
words.definition: Lets the other person speak when you both start talking at once.

examples.en: Oh, sorry, go ahead.
examples.zh: 哦，抱歉，您先说。

words.note: 线上会议很常见，不用尴尬；也可以说 'After you'。

words.term: There's a bit of a lag
words.definition: Explains a delay in audio or video.

examples.en: There's a bit of a lag, so I'll pause for questions now and then.
examples.zh: 有点延迟，所以我会时不时停下来等大家提问。

words.zh: 抱歉迟到了，我是…（迟到时简短道歉并介绍）
words.definition: Apologises briefly and introduces yourself without making a fuss.

examples.en: Sorry I'm late, I'm Sam from the data team. Please carry on.
examples.zh: 抱歉迟到了，我是数据团队的 Sam，你们继续。

words.note: 道歉一句就够，别长篇解释原因，打断会议更尴尬。

words.term: I think we've met before, at …
words.definition: Reconnects with someone you have met, giving a hint about where.

examples.en: I think we've met before, at the Azure meetup last year?
examples.zh: 我们之前好像在去年的 Azure 交流会上见过？

words.term: Sorry, I didn't catch your name
words.zh: 抱歉，刚才没听清您的名字
words.definition: A polite way to ask for someone's name again.

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
examples.zh: 抱歉，刚才没听清您的名字。

words.note: catch = 听清；比 'What's your name again?' 更礼貌。

words.term: How do you pronounce your name?
words.definition: Shows respect by checking how to say someone's name, especially Māori or other non-English names.

examples.en: Before I butcher it, how do you pronounce your name?
examples.zh: 免得我念错，请问您的名字怎么念？

words.note: 新西兰很重视名字读对，尤其毛利名字；问一下是礼貌，不是失礼。

words.term: Remind me, what's your role again?
words.zh: 提醒我一下，您是负责什么的来着？
words.definition: A relaxed way to ask about someone's role when you have forgotten.

examples.en: Sorry, remind me, what's your role again?
examples.zh: 抱歉，提醒我一下，您是负责什么的来着？

words.term: Just to add to that intro, …
words.definition: Adds a detail after someone else has introduced you.

examples.en: Thanks, Mia. Just to add to that intro, I'll also be running the training sessions.
examples.zh: 谢谢 Mia。补充一下，我还会负责培训。

words.zh: 过奖了（别人过度夸你时）
words.definition: A modest response when someone introduces you in an over-the-top way.

examples.en: That's very generous, thanks, Ben. I'm mainly here to help with the data side.
examples.zh: 过奖了，谢谢 Ben。我主要是来帮忙数据这块的。

words.note: 不要否认得太狠（'No, no, I'm not good'），也不要顺势自夸；谢谢后拉回实际角色。

words.zh: 不完全是，其实我是…（别人把你的角色说错时）
words.definition: Politely corrects a wrong description of your role.

examples.en: Not quite — I'm actually on the security side, not networking.
examples.zh: 不完全是，其实我做安全，不是网络。

words.zh: 简单来说，我…（头衔太模糊时）
words.definition: Explains your job in everyday words when your title is vague or full of jargon.

examples.en: My title's 'platform engineer'. In plain terms, I build and look after the systems the developers use.
examples.zh: 我的头衔是平台工程师。简单来说，我搭建和维护开发人员用的系统。

words.term: Given we're short on time, I'll just say …
words.definition: Keeps your intro very short when the meeting is running late.

examples.en: Given we're short on time, I'll just say I'm Raj and I'm doing the testing.
examples.zh: 时间紧，我就简单说一句：我是 Raj，负责测试。

words.definition: A friendly way to start talking to someone you don't know at a meeting.

examples.en: I don't think we've met — I'm Lucy, the business analyst.
examples.zh: 我们好像还没见过，我是业务分析师 Lucy。

words.definition: Apologises for interrupting someone.

examples.en: Sorry, I've jumped in there. You go first.
examples.zh: 抱歉我插话了，您先说。

words.term: Sorry, I missed the start of the intros
words.zh: 抱歉，开头的介绍我错过了
words.definition: Explains you came in late and may need people to repeat their names.

examples.en: Sorry, I missed the start of the intros. I'm Tom, from the vendor side.
examples.zh: 抱歉，开头的介绍我错过了。我是乙方的 Tom。

words.term: Happy to go into more detail later
words.definition: Keeps your intro short when someone starts asking lots of questions.

examples.en: Happy to go into more detail later, but in short, I'll be doing the design.
examples.zh: 细节可以之后再聊，简单说就是我负责设计。

words.term: Good question — I'll find out and get back to you
words.zh: 好问题，我确认后再回复您（不确定时别乱答）
words.definition: An honest answer when you don't know something yet.

examples.en: Good question — I'll find out and get back to you by Friday.
examples.zh: 好问题，我确认后周五前回复您。

words.note: 不确定就别猜，这句话在新西兰职场很正常，也显得可靠。

words.zh: 我就介绍到这（简短收尾）
words.definition: A casual, very common way to finish your intro.

examples.en: Anyway, that's me. Over to you, Sarah.
examples.zh: 好，我就介绍到这。Sarah，交给你了。

words.note: 很地道的口语收尾，比 'That's all, thank you' 自然。

words.definition: A slightly longer way to finish your introduction.

examples.en: So that's a bit about me. Happy to answer any questions.
examples.zh: 这就是我的简单介绍，有问题欢迎提。

words.definition: Ends on a positive note about what comes next.

examples.en: Looking forward to getting started next week.
examples.zh: 期待下周开始工作。

words.note: to 后接 -ing 或名词：looking forward to meeting，不要说 to meet。

words.definition: Promises to send something after the meeting; common in NZ.

examples.en: I'll send through my contact details and the slides after this.
examples.zh: 会后我把联系方式和幻灯片发过来。

words.note: send through 是新西兰常用说法，和 send over 一样。

words.definition: A polite closing when you have met several people for the first time.

examples.en: Nice to meet you all, and see you at the next session.
examples.zh: 很高兴认识大家，下次会议见。

words.term: Great to finally put a face to the name
words.zh: 终于见到真人了（之前只通过邮件或电话）
words.definition: Used when you meet someone you have only emailed or messaged before.

examples.en: Great to finally put a face to the name after all those emails.
examples.zh: 邮件来往了这么久，终于见到真人了。

words.definition: Signals you have finished speaking.

examples.en: I'll leave it there, since I know we've got a full agenda.
examples.zh: 我就说到这儿，知道今天议程很满。

words.term: Any questions for me before we move on?
words.zh: 继续之前，对我有什么问题吗？
words.definition: Invites questions about your role before the meeting continues.

examples.en: Any questions for me before we move on?
examples.zh: 继续之前，有什么想问我的吗？

words.definition: Promises an action after the meeting.

examples.en: I'll follow up with an email so you've got everything in writing.
examples.zh: 我会再发封邮件跟进，把内容都书面写下来。

words.definition: Tells people where to find your contact information.

examples.en: You'll find my details in the meeting invite.
examples.zh: 我的联系方式在会议邀请里。

words.zh: 谢谢、此致（毛利语，常用于邮件结尾）
words.definition: A Māori phrase meaning thanks or regards, very common at the end of work emails in New Zealand.

examples.en: Ngā mihi, Alex
examples.zh: 此致，Alex

words.note: 多用于邮件签名前；口头说 Kia ora 表示感谢更常见。

words.definition: A casual Kiwi way to say thanks at the end of a meeting.

examples.en: Cheers, everyone. Talk soon.
examples.zh: 谢谢大家，回头聊。

words.note: cheers 在新西兰常表示“谢谢”或“再见”，不只是干杯。

words.definition: A friendly, short goodbye at the end of a call.

examples.en: Thanks, Jess. Talk soon.
examples.zh: 谢谢 Jess，回头聊。

words.definition: A casual way to say you will see someone at the next meeting or event.

examples.en: Catch you at the stand-up tomorrow.
examples.zh: 明天站会见。

words.zh: 我把时间交还给…（交还主持人）
words.definition: Returns the floor to the person running the meeting after your intro.

examples.en: That's me, so I'll hand back to Sarah.
examples.zh: 我就说到这，交还给 Sarah。

words.zh: 解决方案架构师（设计整体技术方案）
words.definition: Designs how the whole system will fit together and makes the big technical decisions.

examples.en: I'm the solution architect, so I'll be working out how all the pieces fit together.
examples.zh: 我是解决方案架构师，负责设计各部分怎么组合在一起。

words.zh: 云工程师（搭建和维护云平台）
words.definition: Builds, configures and looks after systems running in the cloud, such as Azure or AWS.

examples.en: I'm a cloud engineer, so I'll be building your Azure environment.
examples.zh: 我是云工程师，会负责搭建你们的 Azure 环境。

words.zh: 数据工程师（搭数据管道和数据仓库）
words.definition: Builds the pipelines and storage that move and prepare data for reporting.

examples.en: I'm a data engineer, which means I get the data from your systems into one place.
examples.zh: 我是数据工程师，也就是把你们各系统的数据集中到一个地方。

words.zh: 数据分析师（分析数据、出结论）
words.definition: Looks at data to answer business questions and explains what the numbers mean.

examples.en: I'm a data analyst, so I'll be digging into the numbers with your finance team.
examples.zh: 我是数据分析师，会和你们财务团队一起深入分析数据。

words.zh: BI 开发（做报表和仪表板）
words.definition: Builds reports and dashboards, often in tools like Power BI.

examples.en: I'm a BI developer, so I'll be building the dashboards you'll see each week.
examples.zh: 我是 BI 开发，你们每周看的仪表板由我来做。

words.note: BI = business intelligence，读作 B-I 两个字母。

words.definition: Works out what the business needs and turns it into clear requirements for the technical team.

examples.en: I'm the business analyst, so I'll be running the workshops to capture your requirements.
examples.zh: 我是业务分析师，会主持研讨会收集你们的需求。

words.note: 常缩写 BA；注意 analyst 读 AN-uh-list。

words.zh: 项目经理（管进度、预算和风险）
words.definition: Plans the project and keeps track of time, budget, risks and who is doing what.

examples.en: I'm the project manager, so I'll be keeping an eye on timelines and budget.
examples.zh: 我是项目经理，负责盯进度和预算。

words.note: 常缩写 PM。

words.zh: 交付负责人（确保项目按承诺交付）
words.definition: Makes sure the team delivers what was promised, on time and to the right quality.

examples.en: I'm the delivery lead, so if anything's off track, I'm the one to talk to.
examples.zh: 我是交付负责人，项目有任何偏差找我就行。

words.zh: 客户经理（维护客户关系和商务）
words.definition: Looks after the relationship with a client, including contracts, renewals and new work.

examples.en: I'm your account manager, so I'll be looking after the commercial side.
examples.zh: 我是你们的客户经理，负责商务方面。

words.note: commercial side = 商务（合同、价格）方面。

words.zh: 服务交付经理（管长期支持服务质量）
words.definition: Makes sure an ongoing support or managed service runs well and meets the agreed service levels.

examples.en: I'm your service delivery manager, so we'll catch up monthly to review how the service is going.
examples.zh: 我是你们的服务交付经理，我们每月会碰一次，回顾服务情况。

words.note: 常缩写 SDM；service levels 指 SLA 约定的服务水平。

words.zh: 技术负责人（带技术团队、把关技术质量）
words.definition: Leads the technical team on a project and makes sure the work is done properly.

examples.en: I'm the technical lead, so I'll be guiding the engineers and reviewing their work.
examples.zh: 我是技术负责人，会指导工程师并审核他们的工作。

words.note: 口语常说 tech lead。

words.zh: 顾问（为客户提供专业建议和实施）
words.definition: An expert who advises clients and often helps them carry out the work.

examples.en: I'm a consultant, mostly working on Microsoft 365 projects.
examples.zh: 我是顾问，主要做 Microsoft 365 项目。

words.note: 注意重音：con-SUL-tant。

words.zh: 首席顾问（资深顾问，常负责复杂项目）
words.definition: A very senior consultant who leads complex work and advises on the big decisions.

examples.en: I'm a principal consultant, so I'll be overseeing the design and stepping in where needed.
examples.zh: 我是首席顾问，负责把关设计，需要时亲自上手。

words.note: principal（首要的）别和 principle（原则）混淆，读音相同。

words.zh: 服务台工程师（一线 IT 支持）
words.definition: Answers calls and tickets from users and fixes everyday IT problems.

examples.en: I'm a service desk analyst, so I'm usually the first person you'll talk to when something breaks.
examples.zh: 我是服务台工程师，出问题时一般第一个跟你们打交道的就是我。

words.note: 也叫 service desk engineer / help desk；level 1 / level 2 表示一线、二线。

words.zh: DevOps 工程师（自动化构建、部署和运维）
words.definition: Automates how software is built, tested and released, and keeps it running smoothly.

examples.en: I'm a DevOps engineer, so I'll be setting up your build and release pipelines.
examples.zh: 我是 DevOps 工程师，会帮你们搭建构建和发布流水线。

words.zh: 安全分析师（监控和处理安全风险）
words.definition: Watches for security threats, investigates alerts and helps keep systems safe.

examples.en: I'm a security analyst, so I'll be reviewing your alerts and access settings.
examples.zh: 我是安全分析师，会检查你们的告警和权限设置。

words.zh: 产品负责人（决定做什么、优先级）
words.definition: Decides what the team should build next and represents the business in an agile team.

examples.en: I'm the product owner, so I'll be setting the priorities for each sprint.
examples.zh: 我是产品负责人，负责确定每个冲刺的优先级。

words.note: 常缩写 PO；敏捷开发中的角色。

words.zh: Scrum Master（敏捷教练，保障团队流程顺畅）
words.definition: Runs the agile ceremonies and helps the team remove anything blocking their work.

examples.en: I'm the scrum master, so I'll be running the stand-ups and clearing any blockers.
examples.zh: 我是 Scrum Master，会主持站会并清除障碍。

words.note: 不是“主管”，不管人，主要服务团队。

words.zh: 利益相关方（受项目影响或有决定权的人）
words.definition: Anyone who is affected by the project or has a say in it.

examples.en: I'm one of the stakeholders on the finance side, so I'll be signing off the reports.
examples.zh: 我是财务方面的相关方之一，报表由我签字确认。

words.note: key stakeholders = 关键相关方；sign off = 审批确认。

words.zh: 联系人（某事项的对接人）
words.definition: The person others should contact first about a particular topic.

examples.en: I'm the main point of contact for anything to do with licensing.
examples.zh: 许可证相关的事，我是主要对接人。

words.note: 缩写 POC；但 POC 也指 proof of concept（概念验证），看上下文。

words.zh: 领域专家（某方面最懂的人，SME）
words.definition: A person who knows a particular area or system really well; often shortened to SME.

examples.en: I've been brought in as the subject matter expert on your payroll system.
examples.zh: 我是作为你们薪资系统的领域专家被请来的。

words.note: SME 读作 S-M-E 三个字母，或读 'smee'。

words.definition: Writes and maintains code for applications and systems.

examples.en: I'm a software developer, mostly working on the back end.
examples.zh: 我是软件开发，主要做后端。

words.note: 也说 developer / dev / software engineer。

words.zh: 网络工程师（管网络、防火墙）
words.definition: Designs and looks after networks, firewalls and connections between sites.

examples.en: I'm a network engineer, so I'll be sorting out the connection between your offices and Azure.
examples.zh: 我是网络工程师，会负责打通你们办公室和 Azure 之间的连接。

words.zh: 系统管理员（维护服务器和账号等）
words.definition: Keeps servers, accounts and core IT systems running day to day.

examples.en: I'm a systems administrator, so I look after your servers and user accounts.
examples.zh: 我是系统管理员，负责你们的服务器和用户账户。

words.note: 口语常说 sysadmin。

words.zh: 平台工程师（搭建开发人员用的内部平台）
words.definition: Builds and runs the shared tools and infrastructure that developers use to ship their work.

examples.en: I'm a platform engineer, so I build the tools that make life easier for our developers.
examples.zh: 我是平台工程师，负责做让开发人员更省事的工具。

words.zh: 测试分析师（设计和执行测试）
words.definition: Plans and runs tests to make sure the system works before users get it.

examples.en: I'm a test analyst, so I'll be writing the test cases and running UAT with your team.
examples.zh: 我是测试分析师，会编写测试用例并和你们团队做用户验收测试。

words.note: 也叫 QA / tester；UAT = user acceptance testing 用户验收测试。

words.zh: 数据科学家（建模、机器学习）
words.definition: Uses statistics and machine learning to find patterns and make predictions from data.

examples.en: I'm a data scientist, so I'll be looking at whether we can forecast demand.
examples.zh: 我是数据科学家，会研究能不能预测需求。

words.zh: 变革管理负责人（帮员工适应新系统）
words.definition: Helps staff adjust to a new system or way of working, through communication and training.

examples.en: I'm the change manager, so I'll make sure your staff are ready for the new system.
examples.zh: 我是变革管理负责人，会确保员工为新系统做好准备。

words.note: IT 运维里的 change manager 也可能指“变更管理”负责人（审批系统变更），看上下文。

words.zh: 售前工程师（售前技术支持）
words.definition: A technical expert who helps the sales team understand the client's needs and shape a solution.

examples.en: I'm a pre-sales engineer, so I'm here to understand your setup before we put a proposal together.
examples.zh: 我是售前工程师，来了解你们的环境，再一起出方案。

words.zh: 项目发起人（客户方高层，拍板和出资）
words.definition: The senior person on the client side who owns the project and makes the final decisions.

examples.en: As the project sponsor, I'll be signing off the key decisions.
examples.zh: 作为项目发起人，关键决策由我拍板。

words.zh: 毕业生岗（刚毕业的新人职位）
words.definition: A role for someone who has recently finished university and is in their first job.

examples.en: I'm a graduate engineer, so I'll be shadowing Raj and helping with the build.
examples.zh: 我是毕业生工程师，会跟着 Raj 学习并协助搭建。

words.note: 常见 graduate programme / grad；shadow sb = 跟着某人学习。
